newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in again, sells dlrs - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in again, sells dlrs - dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Korea intervened again in late Wednesday morning to slow the won's fall, selling dollars in the interbank spot market at around 892.50 won, dealers said.

It was the third central bank intervention on Wednesday. It sold dollars at 892.40 on the spot market in early trading and at around 919 won on the one-year forward market in mid-morning trading, they said.
Bank of Korea officials were unavailable for comment, although a finance ministry official earlier acknowledged the need for steps to prevent the won from falling.
The ministry official, who declined to be identified, also linked the dollar's strength to Tuesday's decision by local banks to bail out the Kia Group, the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate.
The bank's dollar sales immediately pushed the won up to 891.90 won. The local currency soon retreated again and was trading at 892.50 won at 0254 GMT.
